summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, recent CABG and mitral valve replacement, and chronic kidney disease was admitted from rehab with dyspnea, cough, fever, and diarrhea. She was found to have acute congestive heart failure with pulmonary edema, for which she was treated with diuresis. A urine culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, sensitive to piperacillin/tazobactam, and she completed a 7-day antibiotic course. Diarrhea was initially concerning for recurrent C. difficile, but testing was negative; symptoms resolved with supportive care. She developed acute kidney injury likely due to diuretic-induced renal hypoperfusion, prompting a temporary hold on diuresis, with subsequent improvement in renal function. Her warfarin was uptitrated for subtherapeutic INR, and insulin was adjusted for hypoglycemia. She improved clinically, was weaned off oxygen, and discharged back to rehab on furosemide, warfarin, and optimized diabetes regimen with follow-up plans.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
